fixes.where: weddings.html · Reception & Walima · details paragraph 2 ("Hospitality and dietary logistics…")
fixes.what: Cut "halal, vegetarian-only, a dry bar or none of these" and reduce the paragraph to: "The venue's hospitality requirements, the elders served first and who hosts each table: confirmed with your family and the venue before the day."
fixes.why: It is the one place the site reads as catering talk (hard rule) and it is the caterer's brief, not the planner's.

fixes.what: Lead with the families the three slots miss and link them to their own section: "Hindu and Sikh families: haldi and pheras, Anand Karaj. Pakistani, Afghan and Bengali families: nikah, walima, rukhsati." and change the Mehndi & Sangeet caption to "Henna, blessings, music and dancing, for every South Asian family."
fixes.why: The hero promises South Asian but all three slots read Persian/Muslim; a Gujarati or Punjabi mother must see herself before she scrolls, in a 16px stone footnote she will not.

fixes.what: Change "Elders' seats held at the front, at every ceremony." to "Elders seated first, at every ceremony, as the venue and the faith allow."
fixes.why: In a gurdwara the sangat sits on the floor; an absolute "seats at the front" tells Sikh families the planner has not been in one.

fixes.where: how-we-work.html · step 02 and the panel's Consultation line ("Parents and elders included at the level you choose")
fixes.what: Change to "Parents and elders included at the level your family agrees together." in both places (and the FAQ answer "Will you work with our parents directly?").
fixes.why: Parents are often the ones paying and reading; "you choose" addressed to the couple reads as the parents being managed, not welcomed.

fixes.what: Change "We reply within one business day." to "We reply within one business day, by email, or by phone if you leave a number."
fixes.why: A parent who types a number into an optional field wants to know it will be used; it also justifies the field for the couple.

fixes.what: Name the Pakistani entry point the way the Afghan block does: add "For Pakistani families: the nikah, the baraat and the walima, with the rukhsati cued for the elders." after the first sentence.
fixes.why: Afghan families get a labelled block; Pakistani families, the largest Muslim South Asian group in the Bay Area, are only a word in the home footnote.
